Commentary.Commentary: Right then! It was expected to be a one-sided contest and it eventually turned out to be that way in the end. The match has barely lasted 60 overs. Can we get a better contest, come game 2? Let us hope that. Join us for the second ODI on Wednesday, 3rd October, 2018 in Bloemfontein at 1 pm local (1100 GMT). That is a day-night affair. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Victorious South African captain, JP Duminy, like the ones before him, agrees that the pitch behaved stranger than usual. Says that the Kimberley track does a bit in the morning but today, it was a bit more. Is not too worried about his batsmen getting dismissed and puts it down to job done in the end. Is proud of his team for sticking to the game plans and executing them well. And then, he says that it was a difficult wicket to bat upon. On being asked about South Africa trying to play aggressive cricket, Duminy admits that it is a plan but today, it could not quite come off as batting aggressively on this pitch was difficult. (Still, his batsmen kept playing their shots...)

LUNGI NGIDI HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH. He, too, seems surprised by the spice in the wicket. Is happy to register a win after two successive losses in Sri Lanka. On his bowling plans, Lungi feels much confident after the Lankan tour. Stresses that with the surface doing so much, he just needed to put the ball in the right areas. On choosing the right end, Ngidi credits it to Rabada who preferred to run into the wind as the latter likes to challenge himself, giving Lungi the easier option. Having said that, Ngidi also says that he too, would have loved to run into the wind. On his success, he says that he is enjoying international cricket at the moment and hopes to be consistent.

Zimbabwean skipper, Hamilton Masakadza, admits that he was surprised by how the pitch played. Adds that his team did have a look at the surface in the morning and felt that it would do a bit in the first hour but it was difficult to bat on throughout. Laments the poor batting but looking at the track, he feels that had his team got 50-60 more runs, it would have been a great contest. On the remaining matches, he wishes that his batting unit puts more runs on the board.

Now, a word about Zimbabwe's bowling. Could not find too many words to describe their batting. But with the ball, their attitude was impressive. They knew that to win, or even compete, they had to bowl South Africa out and they did so, smartly. One cannot say that they bowled impeccable lines and lengths but they were toying with the ego of the opposition. Tendai Chatara perhaps, could have been given more overs. Please stay tuned for the presentation.

Heinrich Klaasen top scored for South Africa but cannot say that he looked a class apart. He too, played the same type of shots as his other mates did and gifted his wicket as well. Only, he lasted longer than the rest. In the dressing room, the team will be discussing on how can the batting do better next time.

Coming in with an aim of demolishing the opposition bowlers, the home side played more attacking shots than necessary. One can understand their motive but normal cricket could have got them results for their strokes as well. However, they tried to hit out almost each and every ball and as a result - were 4 down for 58. Another wicket there and we would have had a game on our hands.

A look at the match - one side gets bowled out inside 35 overs while the other loses half its unit in chasing a paltry total. But was it really that difficult a pitch? Well, perhaps - there was a shade of uneven bounce here and there. But while Zimbabwe's batsmen lost their wickets to some good bowling, the same cannot be said about the Proteas.

Comfortable win for South Africa. But they nearly made a hash of it. They have registered their BIGGEST ODI WIN over Zimbabwe in terms of balls remaining, but it was a bit of careless cricket from the home side's batsmen.

FOUR! VICTORY FOR SOUTH AFRICA! They have huffed and puffed but have eventually got there. Down the leg side, Mulder just gets a tickle, past the keeper, to the fine leg fence. South Africa win by 5 wickets and 143 balls to spare.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Duminy paddles it fine and gets a boundary. South Africa are a hit away from a win now.
On middle, flicked through the leg side for a run.
Full and around middle, Mulder looks to flick but gets a bit of a leading edge to the off side.
Full and just around off, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Brandon Mavuta is back on. 3-0-18-1 so far.
Shorter and flatter this, punched off the back foot.
Errs in length and lands it shorter of full length, Mulder rocks back and punches it through point, the fielder at sweeper cover does well to run across and restrict the batsmen to just a brace.
Tossed up delivery on off, Duminy skips down the track and drives it to long of for a single.
Mulder flicks it away with a wristy shot and picks up a single.
Fuller on middle, played to mid-wicket to get a run and change strike. Intelligent batting this.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shorter again and is punched through cover-point for a single.
First aggressive instinct by Mulder but fails, luckily he gets beaten on the attempted square cut.
Mulder has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slower and shorter, punched to covers.
Tossed up on off, Duminy plays it through mid-wicket to change strike.
Duminy dances down the track but decides to defend it. Interesting approach this.
FOUR! On the last ball Williams errs in length, Mulder sees it short and wide, goes back and cuts hard through point for a boundary.
JP flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Goes for the sweep again, Duminy adamant here, but again gets rapped on the front pad. He's outside the off stump line again and survives.
Williams fires this one flatter but on Mulder's pads, he works it into the square leg region to get off the mark.
Fuller and slower on the stumps, driven to long on with the spin to pick up a run.
Tossed up delivery around off, Duminy goes down to look for the sweep, misses and gets hit on the pads but outside the line of off. Playing straight is advisable here.
Very full outside off, driven back to the bowler. 12 runs but a wicket as well from the over. Wellington Masakadza's figures read 4-1-24-2.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Willem Mulder is the new man in at number 7, replacing Klaasen.

OUT! Klaasen is gone now. Just a ball before, a man was placed for this shot and the South African wicket-keeper joins his mates in handing one's wicket on a platter. The ball is short and Heinrich goes for the pull again. However, this time, the timing is not quite there and he finds Craig Ervine running in from deep mid-wicket. Easy catch. The on-air commentator says, 'Look at his reaction. He is mortified.' Powerful words. Just 22 more runs needed.
Full and outside off, HK is not enticed into going for the hat-trick. Defends watchfully.
SIX! Save your legs. In a trice, Klaasen has crossed his previous highest score of 43 against India. Another long hop, Heinrich rocks back and pulls it over mid-wicket. A man now goes over there.
SIX! MURDERED! First biggie of the day! A short ball around off, Klaasen goes back and just whip-pulls it. It is a combination of a whip and a pull. Sails over mid-wicket!
Duminy again skips down the track but blocks this short of a length delivery with a straight bat.
Tossed up around off, Klaasen leans ahead and drives through mid off to get another single.

Leg Bye. Duminy looks to go down for the sweep, sees the length is not suitable for the shot and tries to turn this into the leg side. The ball spins in and hits him on the pads as the batsmen set off for a run. An appeal from Zimbabwe but turned down by the umpire. Seems to be going down the leg.
Defended off the front foot by JP presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower and fuller on off, driven down to long off to change strike.
Tossed up on the stumps, worked into the mid-wicket region.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Duminy dances down the track again and does well to block the ball.
Duminy comes down the track to this short of a length ball, blocks it into the off side.
Short ball, pulled into mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! The problem with Zimbabwe is that there is at least one bad ball every over which is dispatched by the batsmen and they are not allowing to build some pressure. Dishes this one on his pads, Klaasen nudges it fine into the leg side and gets a boundary.
Duminy again gives the charge, seeing him come forward Jarvis pulls his length back a bit. Duminy is good enough though to punch it into the cover region to get a run.
Dances down the track and drives to mid on for a single and retains strike. Duminy gets to his 5000th ODI run with this, he is the 9th South African to do so.
Williams fires this one on the pads, Duminy tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Klaasen rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball, the batsmen have run through for a single.
William flights this and keeps it full, Duminy keeps it out with a straight bat.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A bit quicker and flatter this time around off, Klaasen makes room and tries to cut but is beaten by pace and misses the shot.
Tossed up on off, comes forward and blocks it out.
Duminy has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A hat-trick of beats. A bit fuller around off this, Duminy goes for the drive this time and again gets beaten.

Beauty again! Similar delivery, a bit fuller may be. Duminy again looks to play at it but gets beaten due to the away movement. Jarvis is a bit unlucky here but he needs to be patient and continue with the same line and length.

Peach! Excellent from Jarvis, he needs to be consistent there. He lands this a bit short of good length around off, it has an away shape to it from over the wicket, Duminy looking to play at it gets beaten and survives.
A length ball around off, tucked through square leg for a single.
FOUR! Errs in length again and pays the price again. Duminy this time sees the short and wide ball and cuts it superbly through point for his first boundary.
Tossed up ball on off, Klaasen strides forward and drives it to long off to cross over.
Klaasen shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Excellent from Klaasen. He sees the ball fractionally short on leg, goes back and across and pulls it over mid-wicket for another boundary.
Klaasen has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up delivery on off, Duminy goes back and works it into the square leg region for a single.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.

FOUR! Swatted! Misses his length and the price is 4 runs. He bangs it in on the off stump line. The pace and height on this one is perfect for the pull shot and Klaasen does exactly that, sending it whistling through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Klaasen stands tall and punches this shortish ball on off to covers.
A bit shorter of a good length but is wide of off, Klaasen shoulders arms.
Fuller length, driven back to the bowler.
On a length outside off, punched towards mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground to end a  good over from Mavuta.
Duminy defends it from within the crease.

Lucky escape! Full and around middle and leg, Duminy goes low and across the off stump and looks to scoop this one over the keeper. However, he gets an inside edge onto his pads and the ball lobs in the air. There is a man at backward square leg but he cannot get there! Wow. That would have been terrific for Zimbabwe - 2 wickets in 2 balls.
The batsmen keep coming and going. Here's the next. Skipper JP Duminy.

OUT! That is totally irresponsible and immature. Inexperience at show here. But Zimbabwe will not mind. Mavuta tosses this one and lands it full around the middle and leg stump line. Jonker, in aggressive mode for reasons unknown, tries to flick this uppishly through mid-wicket but hits it towards Williams there. He gets low to his left and takes a good catch. South Africa need to be careful now, they are 4 down. Game on? Still 60 needed.
Flat and straight, Jonker tries to flick it but misses to get hit on the pads.
Mavuta flights this and lands it on middle and leg, driven to covers.

Dropped just short of point. Jarvis keeps this a bit shorter of good length outside off, Jonker cuts it but mistimes it completely. The ball lobs towards point where the fielder dives in front to catch it but does not quite reach it and stops it on the bounce.
Better from Jarvis as he dishes this one on a length attacking the stumps. Klaasen tucks it into the mid-wicket region for a run.
A bit fuller this but still a bit outside off stump. Klaasen makes a good leave.
Lands this on a length a bit wide of off, Klaasen already scored a boundary in the over does not take any risk and shoulders arms.
FOUR! Smack! You cannot miss your length, especially at this pace. Klaasen accepts the gift and pulls it through mid-wicket to earn a boundary.
Marginally shorter of a good length on off, punched to covers.
Kyle Jarvis to bowl from the other end. 3-0-20-0 so far.
Short again on middle, Jonker pulls through the deep square leg region to pick up a a brace.
Short again and Jonker goes for the pull, loses his balance as the ball hits his body and rolls down into the on side.
Tossed up and very full, defended off the front foot.
FOUR! Too short and punished. Jonker sees this one shorter in length, rocks back and pulls through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, kept out.
Keeps the leg spinner a bit shorter in length on middle, Klaasen goes back and punches it to loing off for a single.

No, I am not sleepy. We rarely see players taking a Lunch break in one-day cricket. But this match has progressed so quickly that we are already done with nearly 70 percent of the game. The Proteas need just 73 more runs to win but can Zimbabwe get the same energy levels which they had before the break? Here's the debutant and former Under-19 captain - Brandon Mavuta. Klaasen to face.
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

So we go into a bit of a break now. Zimbabwe will not be too happy. They were into a bit of a groove and would have fancied getting into the Protean middle order, had they been playing for another 5 overs. Will South Africa bat a bit more sensibly after the break? Join us back at 1415 local (1215 GMT) to find out.

Andile Phehlukwayo is having a chat with Shaun Pollock. The former says that he is very happy with his display today. Reckons that it is a very good wicket for the seamers and he just tried to hit his lengths consistently. Praises the entire bowling unit for being on the mark right from the go. On bowling from both ends, Andile smiles and says that it was very tough bowling into the wind. But credits the management for giving the team lessons on how to bowl into the wind, before this game. The advice was to not run in but just jog through, he informs. On the team chasing the total, he reckons that the batsmen just need to apply themselves and hit through the line. On being further asked whether he would fancy batting on this surface, Phehlukwayo laughs and hopes that he does not get a chance to bat!

Zimbabwe have bowled well but South Africa have simply not been patient. They have tried to dictate terms just for the sake of it. And the result is there for us to see. Had this been some other opponent, it could have been a very dicey game for the home side.

An interesting passage of play! One would have thought that the South African openers would have liked to establish their dominance in this 45-minute session. But what has transpired is - they have ended up losing 3 wickets. And we have seen everything - dismissals, dropped catches and even no balls.
A shortish delivery on off is played towards point. THAT'S LUNCH.
On a good length around off, this time he cracks the drive but straight to covers.
A full length ball is driven through to mid on.

Beaten! Not a very smart shot this by Jonker. They are 3 down and very close to the lunch interval. He needs to be a bit more cautious here. Chatara lands this fractionally shorter of a good length delivery outside off. Jonker, who showed good patience in the beginning of the over goes for a flashy drive through off, but the extra bounce beats his bat.
Wide! Strays down leg, Jonker tries to flick but misses. Wide given.
After losing 3 wickets it seems the Proteas will be a bit more patient chasing this. Jonker leaves this one outside off.
Jonker lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Driven through mid on by Heinrich.
FOUR! Masakadza misses his length fractionally and lands it a bit short, Klaasen rocks back quickly and fiercely cuts this through point for a boundary.
Slower and fuller ball on off is driven to covers.
Klaasen has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up on off, defended off the front foot.
Christiaan Jonker is the new man in. Around 3 minutes to go for Lunch.

OUT! Markram is not lucky for the third time. This is not dropped. This is not a no ball. Zimbabwe have struck thrice before Lunch. Full and outside off, Aiden does not care whether the break is coming or not. He is in the mood to attack and does not spare this one either. Looks to clear mid off but the ball hits the toe end of his bat. Goes straight to mid off where Elton Chigumbura takes it easily. Poor choice of a shot from Markram. He could have waited for a while and come back after the break.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
A length ball outside off, Markram now being very watchful having being given the reprieve. He lets it go by.
Similar length but angling into middle stump line, Markram turns it to mid-wicket.
Chatara fires this one way outside off to entice Markram into a shot.
Nothing on the Free Hit. A low full toss, pushed towards mid on.
The Free Hit is coming up. Where will this be deposited?

EDGED AND TAKEN! But it is a no ball! Oh dear... A length ball, outside off, Markram gives it the kitchen sink and gets a thick outside edge, as there is no footwork. Also, there is extra bounce too, as we have seen throughout the morning. The ball goes straight to first slip where the catch is taken but here comes the drama. They check for the overstepping and replays show that CHATARA HAS CROSSED THE LINE! What a reprieve for Aiden. First, the dropped catch. Now, this.
Punched off the back foot by Klaasen to end the over.
Aiden skips down the track and drives this to the right of mid on for a single.
FOUR! A short and wide delivery is dealt with perfectly. Markram rocks back and cuts this through point for a cracking boundary.
Full and around leg stump, pushed down the ground to long off for a run.
Short and outside off, Klaasen goes back and punches it through the covers to get off the mark with a couple.
A touch short outside off, punched back to the bowler.
A straighter ball, Markram looks to push at it but gets hit on the pads.
Markram rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Aiden rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

FOUR! Smashing square drive by Markram. He reaches out to this length ball wide of off and goes for the booming drive again to get a boundary. He's come out with an attacking mindset. This time the timing is good enough to take the ball across the ropes.
Aiden has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Dishes this one on a good length but wide of off, seeing the width on offer, Markram flays at this one and gets it past the cover-point region for a brace.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.

NOT OUT. The foot never left the crease. Full and outside off, Klaasen looks to sweep but misses. The keeper whips off the bails and appeals. It is referred upstairs but replays show that the foot was planted firmly ever since the shot was played.
STUMPING APPEAL! OUT? NOT OUT? Referred upstairs...
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Heinrich Klaasen walks in at number 4, replacing Hendricks.

OUT! Right through and Zimbabwe have taken 2! Lovely bowling from Masakadza but absolutely no technique from Reeza. This is landed on middle, RH lunges to defend but is nowhere to the pitch of the ball. The bat is not even close to the ball and is closer to the pad. Was he expecting the arm ball? Perhaps. But it isn't the arm ball. It spins away, past the outside edge and hits the timber. Wellington is excited, to say the least.
Misses out. Short and outside off, Hendricks cuts it towards cover.
Outside off, Hendricks comes forward to push but is beaten by the ball spinning away.
Spin is introduced early. Wellington Masakadza to bowl now.
A good length ball on off, tapped to point for a single.

DROPPED! Chatara's persistence on that tight line and length almost reaped rewards. A good length ball around off, Aiden goes for the big booming cover drive on the up. The ball bounces more than he expects as it takes the outside edge and flies high to the right of Taylor. He leaps across and gets his right glove to it but cannot pouch it. Should he have left it for the fielder at first slip? Maybe that guy would have had a better chance. Zimbabwe need to take these half chances if they want to compete today.
Chatara again dishes this wide of the off stump line, Markram shoulders arms.
Wide of off again, Markram leaves this watchfully.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Markram though takes a big stride forward to keep it out.
Short of a good length delivery outside off, Markram leaves it alone.
FOUR! What a way to get off the mark! A length ball, outside off, Hendricks gets on his toes and just punches it through the covers. Away she goes, to the boundary.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! IMPERIOUS! What a shot. Fractionally short in length, outside off, Markram cuts it through point and there is no one to stop that.
On a length around off, nipping back in sharply, Markram looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
A length ball on middle, defended towards short mid-wicket.

Reeza lets the ball go behind outside his off stump. A good over comes to an end, a wicket off the first ball of the over and one more which almost got another wicket on the penultimate delivery as well.

Cut in half! A jaffa this from Chatara. He lands this a bit short of a length around off. Markram from within his crease tries to block it but the ball hits the deck and deviates inward prodigiously cutting him in half. The ball has missed everything and Aiden survives but the keeper fails to stop it cleanly. A bye results. The visitors needs to bowl more of these.
Straight ball played through mid-wicket by Aiden.
A bit outside off on a length, Markram tries to put bat on ball but misses.
Markram has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Reeza Hendricks walks in at number 3, replacing Elgar.

OUT! Wild slog and a wicket gifted! Elgar, against the run of play, skips down the track on the very first ball of the fourth over. He looks to swat the length ball angling into his body through mid-wicket. But takes his eyes off it and his head moves while he is trying to whack it too hard. As a result, the ball flies off the leading edge to third man where Moor pouches it with his fingers pointing up.

FOUR! Creamed through covers! Jarvis looking to find some movement in the air pitches this full just outside off, Markram leans forward and drives this wonderfully through covers for a superb boundary.
This time he waits for the ball a bit longer and guides it towards point with an open face to pinch a single and gets off strike.
On a tight line and length around off, Elgar strides ahead and keeps it out with no problems.
Jarvis fires this a bit straight, angling into Dean, Elgar tucks it into the mid-wicket region.
A good length ball around off is defended solidly off the front foot.
Elgar has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Keeps it very full attacking the stumps, driven back to the bowler. Ends a tight over, just a wide and a single off it.
Fires this very wide of off, Markram shoulders arms.
Good running by the Proteas, Dean drives this to the right of mid off and takes a quick single.
A repeat of the previous delivery and played similarly by Elgar into mid-wicket.
A good length ball angling into the batsman from over the wicket, Elgar gets cramped but keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Corrects his line and lands a short of a length delivery on off, Elgar keeps it out off the back foot.
Wide! Tendai starts off with a wide down the leg side.
Tendai Chatara to bowl with the second new ball.
Wide of off, left alone.
Outside off again, Markram does not flirt with it and lets it go.
Markram lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Markram punches this short of a length delivery through covers to get a brace.

FOUR! Close shave! Exactly like that, keeps this a bit shorter of a good length around off, the ball takes off on landing. The ball takes the edge as Markram looks to play at it and it flies past the second slip fielder. First boundary for the Proteas but not a convincing one.
A short of a length ball angling into the batsman is tucked into mid-wicket. Good bounce seen there. They have to make use of it though.
We are back for the chase. Dean Elgar and Aiden Markram to open the batting for South Africa. Kyle Jarvis to steam in with the first new ball. Markram on strike. Two slips in place. Here we go...
